assessment.answer: The score of 0.688 comes mainly from a deep annualized net loss ($101.2M, about 104% of assets) and operating cash burn ($88.6M) set against only $97.6M of assets, liabilities at 80% of assets (peer median 46%) and a current ratio of 1.05 (peer median 3.26). The filing text is worse than the numbers suggest: management has substantial going concern doubt, says cash lasts only into Q4 2025, and states it has explored and will keep exploring a bankruptcy filing, while no Fabry partner has been signed and Nasdaq delisting is a live threat. The score reflects real distress, and if anything the 0.5-0.7 band's 4% base rate understates it.
moved_by: Management explicitly says it has explored, and will continue to explore, filing for bankruptcy protection (10-Q 2025-08-07, repeated from the 10-K and Q1 10-Q)

Cash runway only into Q4 2025: about $47.2M ($38.3M cash plus $8.9M post-quarter ATM) against a reported Q2 operating burn of about $18.2M, or about $36M a quarter without the one-time $18.0M Lilly upfront. That is roughly 4 to 8 months, with R&D expected to rise
No Fabry commercialization partner yet, which management calls key to raising capital; Pfizer, Biogen, Novartis and Kite collaborations have all ended
Repeat Nasdaq minimum bid price deficiency with a compliance date of 2025-10-27, which would make equity raising harder
Against: no debt, so no lender can force a filing; ATM capacity of $168.8M remains; $21.1M May 2025 offering and $18.0M Lilly upfront show the company can still raise money

reasons.quote: Pfizer will not be obligated to pay the Company the remaining milestone payments and royalties.

reasons.reason: Cash needs are set to rise because of Fabry BLA work
reasons.quote: We expect research and development expenses to increase in the near-term due to Fabry disease program BLA readiness activities

reasons.reason: Nasdaq listing at risk, which would impair the equity raising the company depends on
reasons.numbers: $1.00 minimum bid; compliance date 2025-10-27; repeat of the 2024 deficiency
reasons.quote: We currently do not meet, and may not regain compliance with, the listing standards of the Nasdaq Capital Market, and as a result our common stock may be delisted.

reasons.reason: Most of the loss is cash-driven, so it is not an artefact of impairments
reasons.numbers: stock-based compensation $4.8M; D&A $2.0M; ROU amortization $1.8M; no impairment in 2025; FX loss $3.6M
reasons.source: 10-Q, 2025-08-07, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows

evidence_against.point: No borrowings, so there are no covenants, maturities or lenders who could force a filing. A filing would be the company's own choice once it runs out of cash
evidence_against.quote: raise funding through debt financing; and

evidence_against.point: Large remaining ATM capacity, and the company keeps selling shares through it
evidence_against.quote: Approximately $168.8 million remained available under the sales agreement as of June 30, 2025.

evidence_against.point: Raised $21.1M in a May 2025 underwritten offering, showing access to capital despite going concern doubt
evidence_against.quote: We received aggregate net proceeds of $21.1 million, after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions of $1.4 million and other offering costs of $0.5 million.

evidence_against.point: New Lilly capsid license brought $18.0M upfront, with up to $1.4B in potential milestones; earlier Genentech and Astellas capsid deals also brought cash
evidence_against.quote: Under the Lilly Agreement, the Company received an $18.0 million upfront license payment in April 2025.
Subsequent to June 30, 2025, the Company sold 17,250,862 shares of its common stock under the Open Market Sale Agreement℠ with Jefferies, for net proceeds of approximately $8.9 million.

evidence_against.point: Losses and burn have narrowed a lot from the prior year, and equity recovered from $4.9M to $19.6M during the quarter
The company has repeatedly extended its runway: the 10-K said cash would last only into mid-Q2 2025, and it is still operating, now guiding into Q4 2025
evidence_against.quote: we expect to meet our liquidity requirements only into the middle of the second quarter of 2025.

evidence_against.point: The deficiency notice had no immediate effect on listing, and a second 180-day period may be available
evidence_against.quote: The Notice has no immediate effect on the listing of the Company’s common stock on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

evidence_against.point: No missed payments, defaults, forbearance, restructuring advisors or late filings reported

timeline.event: First Nasdaq minimum bid price deficiency notice (Global Select Market)
8-K: stockholders approved raising authorized shares from 640M to 960M
8-K: Pfizer terminates the hemophilia A collaboration for convenience, effective 2025-04-21
10-K: going concern doubt, runway only into mid-Q2 2025, bankruptcy filing being explored
Pfizer termination effective; no further milestones or royalties
Second Nasdaq bid price deficiency notice; compliance deadline 2025-10-27
Q1 10-Q: Lilly license with $18.0M upfront, equity $4.9M, runway only early into Q3 2025
Annual meeting: equity plan increase and directors approved with notable opposition
Quarter end: cash $38.3M, equity $19.6M after the May underwritten offering ($21.1M net) and ATM sales
Q2 10-Q: going concern doubt, runway into Q4 2025, bankruptcy still being explored, $8.9M post-quarter ATM proceeds

dates_to_watch: 2025-10-27: Nasdaq minimum bid price compliance deadline (reverse split or second 180-day period)
Q4 2025: the point at which management says current cash runs out
Q3 2025 10-Q (around November 2025): updated runway and going concern language
Any announcement of a Fabry commercialization partner or new financing
Any 8-K naming restructuring advisors or a strategic alternatives process
would_change_my_mind: A signed Fabry commercialization deal with meaningful upfront cash
A sizeable equity or royalty financing that extends runway well into 2026
New capsid license deals or Lilly milestones bringing in cash
Regaining Nasdaq compliance without losing access to the ATM
Toward more risk: hiring restructuring advisors, failure to raise money before Q4 2025, or delisting
could_not_check: Exact Q2 2025 cash burn without the Lilly upfront (derived as six-month minus Q1 operating cash flow, then adjusted)
Current share price and how much more ATM selling the market can absorb
Terms and remaining value of the Astellas and Genentech deals beyond what the findings state
Lease obligations and other off-balance-sheet commitments that would count in a bankruptcy
Status of Fabry partnering talks and the FDA/BLA timeline
